newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares rise on reform decree, no fall seen.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares rise on reform decree, no fall seen.

text.p: Leading Russian shares rose on Monday, boosted by a series of presidential decrees on natural monopoly reform, traders said, predicting prices would be steady or firm between market holidays over the next two weeks.
The Russian Trading System of 22 shares rose 1.3 percent to close at 301.54 on limp total market turnover of $19.2 million. The index closed on Friday at 297.60. It last closed above 300 on April 9.
Some traders said investors were trying to stake positions before market holidays on May 1-4 and May 9-11.
"Everyone wants to invest before the holidays, even more so because there will be a rise because of a shortage of offers," Creditanstalt-Grant senior trader Andrei Galperin said.
Many brokers will take off much of the holidays, making shares harder to find.
The president signed a decree on restructuring natural monopolies, industries which by their nature have no competitors, such as gas and electricity, telecoms and railways.

First Prime Minister Boris Nemtsov, who is leading the reform campaign, said gas producer Gazprom and national power utility UES would not be broken up, and the state would retain 51 percent of UES shares.
"For UES and Gazprom today, it really was good news and the market reacted duly," said Galperin.
UES rose to $0.2305 from $0.2262 on Friday, while Gazprom fell to $0.6380 from $0.6675 on Friday, although ask/bid prices remained at Friday's levels of $0.640/$0.659.

Yeltsin also confirmed in a decree that a 49 percent stake in Svyazinvest, the national telecoms holding company, would be sold -- 24 percent in an investment tender for Russian investors and 25 percent plus one share in a sale open to foreigners also.

Svyazinvest chairman Nail Izmailov said last week that the president would sign a decree within 10 days which would detail plans for transferring a 38 percent stake in international long-distance telecom Rostelekom to Svyazinvest.
The president's press service was unable to confirm Monday's decree included the Rostelekom transfer but Rostelekom edged up to $3.53 from $3.50 on Friday.
"Demand clearly dominated on the market today, and UES pulled it along behind it," said Regent European Securities trader Alexander Fonarkov.
Traders said they saw interest from both Russian and Western players.
"There is interest from the West, but there's actually not a great deal of money on the market. The situation will be quiet at least until the middle of May," said Fonarkov.
"I don't think this is the summer rise yet," he said, referring to the growth which traders have predicted by late May or June.
